search_strategy: Systematic and thorough, source-by-source: wiki first (whole-page fetch including comments -- correctly noted BookStack search does not index comments and fetched pages 132/133/134 whole via /api/pages/{id}), then Gitea issues (none found), then mail (per-thread IMAP fetch by id range, eventually listing all 142 headers and reading every plausible thread), then Mattermost -- first via the search API for a handful of terms (output_cap, max_output_bytes, elided, truncated_streams), then by dumping the ENTIRE chat history (10181 lines, all 9 channels, page through channels/{id}/posts) to a local file and grepping/sed-ing clusters around every hit. This bulk-dump-then-grep approach recovered the large majority of remarks (29/38 clues, all 4 herrings, all 4 reversals) but has a systematic blind spot: a remark whose exact wording never intersects the chosen grep vocabulary is invisible even though it is sitting in the local dump. All 9 missed clues fit this pattern -- none of them contain 'output_cap', 'max_output_bytes', 'elided', 'MIN_MAX', or 'truncated_streams' verbatim. Three of the nine (l-floor-nikolai, say26, l-floor-konrad, all in #cookbooks/#incidents) happen to be the only remarks naming OutputCapError, field_validator/ValidationError, and the .max_bytes attribute + exact message text -- exactly the vocabulary the failed grader assertion needs. The agent never grepped for generic terms like 'cap', 'floor', 'ValueError', or 'warning' that would have caught these.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally with a high reward (0.8889/1.0, 8 of 9 facts). Pushed to main (commit bdcb8e5), CI green, deploy step ran and confirmed. Only g2.r1.failure_behavior scored 0, due to an ImportError on `OutputCapError` (the agent's class is named `InvalidOutputBudgetError`).
notable: The agent self-caught and fixed a real double-logging bug with zero corpus guidance: after pushing its first commit, it noticed on its own that the except-path salvage cap would re-log a truncation warning already logged in the try block (e.g. when Sandbox.__exit__ raises after a successful capped return), and shipped a second commit (bdcb8e5, 'announce each capped stream once per sandbox run') adding an `announced: set` de-dupe. This exactly matches the answer key's 'the salvage cap in except Exception: none' requirement, but was derived from re-reasoning about its own code, not from any remark (transcript lines 5900-6050 in the full JSON, messages 183-188).

Bulk grep-dump search strategy (10181-line full chat.txt, grepped for ~7 fixed terms) is efficient but has a hard blind spot: any remark whose exact wording doesn't contain one of the searched terms is invisible even though it's sitting in the local file. All 9 missed clues fit this pattern exactly.

The three remarks the agent needed most for the lost fact (g2.r1.l-floor-nikolai, g2.r1.say26, g2.r1.l-floor-konrad -- OutputCapError, field_validator, and .max_bytes + exact message) sit in #cookbooks and #incidents, two of the three lowest-traffic channels in the corpus (2 and 6 remarks total respectively), which may partly explain why they never surfaced in high-volume keyword-based passes over #pipeline/#code-review/#engineering.

The agent correctly treated wiki pages 132/133 (about error_truncated) as answering a NEIGHBOURING question rather than contradicting the ticket -- exactly the reading the ticket's own guidance instructs ('a page that looks like it contradicts the ticket is nearly always about a neighbouring question'), transcript line 1241.

Despite never seeing OutputCapError, the agent's own test suite (test_output_cap.py, 17/17 passing) gave it false confidence that failure_behavior was fully correct -- its tests check InvalidOutputBudgetError against its own invented name/message, so nothing locally signalled the naming mismatch before submission.
